'''Romeo James Langford''' (born October 25, 1999) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for [[BCM Gravelines-Dunkerque]] of the French [[LNB Élite]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana Hoosiers]] and was ranked as one of the highest prospects in the college class of 2019, as he finished as the fifth overall prospect in the 2018 247sports rankings. A shooting guard, he was drafted by the [[Boston Celtics]] 14th overall in the [[2019 NBA draft]].<ref name=LangfordDecision>{{cite web|first=Kyle|last=Neddenriep|title=Romeo Langford decision: Mr. Basketball picks IU|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2018/04/30/langford-announcement/559263002/|work=Indianapolis Star|date=April 30, 2018|access-date=April 30, 2018}}</ref>

==High school career==
Langford attended [[New Albany High School (Indiana)|New Albany High School]]. Despite substantial interest from multiple prep schools, Langford chose to spend his four high school years at New Albany.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/preps/indiana/2017/11/27/romeo-langford-never-considered-leaving-new-albany/898417001/ |title=Romeo Langford says he never considered leaving New Albany for a prep school |work=[[The Courier-Journal]] |date= November 27, 2017 |access-date= November 27, 2017 |last=Winstead |first=Kenzie}}</ref> As a freshman, Langford led New Albany to a 23–3 record and the regional tournament while averaging 17.1 [[Point (basketball)|points]] and 6.0 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2016/03/16/total-package-langford-drawing-comparisons-bailey/81863476/ |title='Total package' Romeo Langford drawing comparisons to Damon Bailey |work=[[The Indianapolis Star|Indy Star]] |date= March 16, 2016 |access-date= November 28, 2017 |last=Neddenriep |first=Kyle}}</ref> In his sophomore year, he averaged 30.2 points, 9.0 rebounds, and 3.0 [[Assist (basketball)|assists]] per game while leading New Albany to a 27–1 record and a class 4A state championship, the team's first state title since 1973. In his junior year, he averaged 28.7 points, 8.9 rebounds, and 3.4 assists per game, leading New Albany to a 25–4 record and to the class 4A state quarterfinals. On November 21, 2017, Langford opened up his senior season with a then career high 48 points in a 110–36 victory over Charlestown.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.slamonline.com/college-hs/high-school/top-5-recruit-romeo-langford-drops-48-points/#H0LK42JubA42HelT.97 |title=Top 5 Recruit Romeo Langford Drops 48 Points |work=[[Slam (magazine)|SlamOnline.com]] |date= November 22, 2017 |access-date= November 25, 2017}}</ref> On February 1, Langford scored a new career high 63 points against Jennings County. On January 16, 2018, Langford was announced as a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] to participate in the [[2018 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2018 game]].,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://kwese.espn.com/recruiting/basketball/story/_/id/22122836/rj-barrett-zion-williamson-lead-mcdonald-all-american-teams |title=Top players named to McDonald's All-American teams |date= January 16, 2018 |access-date= January 16, 2018 |last= Borzello |first= Jeff |work=[[ESPN]]}}</ref> where he competed and won the Legends and Stars Shootout competition.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.newsandtribune.com/sports/high-school-basketball-langford-s-half-court-shot-helps-team/article_ca22df9e-316a-11e8-93ae-33f4083a2c47.html|title=HIGH SCHOOL BASKETBALL: Langford's half-court shot helps team to win|last=COOK|first=JOSH|work=News and Tribune|access-date=April 4, 2018|language=en}}</ref> Langford finished his high school career fourth on the all-time Indiana state scoring list with 3,002 points.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2018/03/17/thanks-romeo-new-albany-stars-storied-high-school-career-comes-sudden-end/432357002/ |title='Thanks, Romeo': New Albany star's storied high school career comes to sudden end |date= March 17, 2018 |access-date= March 28, 2018 |first=Kyle |last=Neddenriep |work=[[The Indianapolis Star|Indy Star]]}}</ref> The penultimate award of his high school career, Langford was crowned [[Indiana Mr. Basketball]] of 2018 at the annual IndyStar Sports Awards ceremony. In addition, he was also named the Boys Athlete of the Year.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2018/04/29/romeo-langford-wins-indiana-mr-basketball-indiana-sports-awards/559072002/|title=Romeo Langford of New Albany earns IndyStar Indiana Mr. Basketball|date=April 29, 2018 |access-date=April 29, 2018 |first=Kyle |last=Neddenriep |work=[[The Indianapolis Star|Indy Star]]}}</ref>

===Recruitment===
Langford was rated as a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]], [[247Sports.com|247Sports]], [[Scout.com|Scouts]], and [[ESPN]], which  praised him for his electric scoring and playmaking abilities.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.news-sentinel.com/sports/2017/12/11/romeo-langford-series-managing-the-circus/ |title=NS on Romeo Langford, Part I: Managing the circus |date= December 11, 2017 |access-date= December 13, 2017 |work=[[The News-Sentinel]] |first=Tom |last=Davis}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.news-sentinel.com/sports/2017/12/12/ns-on-romeo-langford-part-ii-is-defending-the-states-top-player-even-possible/ |title=NS on Romeo Langford, Part II: Is defending the state's top player even possible? |date= December 12, 2017 |access-date= December 13, 2017 |work=[[The News-Sentinel]] |first=Tom |last=Davis}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.news-sentinel.com/sports/2017/12/13/ns-on-romeo-langford-part-iii-why-he-should-go-anywhere-but-indiana-university/ |title=NS on Romeo Langford, Part III: Why he should go anywhere but Indiana University |date= December 13, 2017 |access-date= December 13, 2017 |work=[[The News-Sentinel]] |first=Dan |last=Vance}}</ref>

Langford was recruited in high school by numerous high-profile schools, including [[University of Indiana|Indiana]], [[University of Louisville|Louisville]],
[[University of Kansas|Kansas]], [[University of Kentucky|Kentucky]], [[Vanderbilt University|Vanderbilt]], [[University of North Carolina|North Carolina]], [[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA]], and [[Duke University|Duke]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2017/04/07/battle-romeo-langford/100173088/ |title=The Battle for Romeo Langford is on |work=[[The Indianapolis Star|IndyStar]] |date= April 9, 2017 |access-date= November 26, 2017 |last=Neddenriep |first=Kyle}}</ref> and was visited by multiple coaches including [[John Calipari]], [[Bill Self]], [[Roy Williams (coach)|Roy Williams]], and [[Archie Miller (basketball)|Archie Miller]].<ref name=Langfordinterview /><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/indiana/2017/12/08/indiana-archie-miller-romeo-langford-new-albany-floyd-central/936803001/ |title=Indiana coach Archie Miller checks out Romeo Langford in New Albany-Floyd Central game |work=[[The Courier-Journal]]
|date= December 8, 2017 |access-date= December 9, 2017 |first=Gentry |last=Estes}}</ref> On November 11, 2017, Langford announced via [[Twitter]] that he had narrowed his choices down to Indiana, Kansas, and Vanderbilt.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.crimsonquarry.com/2017/11/11/16637718/romeo-langford-trims-his-list-to-indiana-vanderbilt-and-kansas |title=Romeo Langford trims his list to Indiana, Vanderbilt, and Kansas |date= November 11, 2017 |access-date= November 21, 2017 |last=Grossman |first=Jack}}</ref> When asked about a timeline for his decision, Langford emphasized that he didn't want to rush the decision, and that he would "probably be making [his] decision after the season."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://scout.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/QA-with-five-star-guard-Romeo-Langford-108660549 |title=Q and A with Five Star Guard Romeo Langford |date= October 9, 2017 |access-date= November 21, 2017 |work=[[Scout.com]] |last=Daniels |first=Evan}}</ref> Langford announced on April 11, 2018, that he would declare his college choice on April 30 at New Albany High School.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/recruiting/2018/04/11/romeo-langford-announces-date-college-decision-kansas-vanderbilt-indiana/508086002/ |title=Romeo Langford announces date for college pick between Kansas, Vanderbilt and Indiana |date= April 11, 2018 |access-date= April 19, 2018 |work=courier-journal.com |last=Page |first=Fletcher}}</ref> On April 30, 2018, he announced his intention to play for his home state Indiana University.<ref name=LangfordDecision /> He is the 27th former Indiana Mr. Basketball and 21st former McDonald's All-American to play basketball at Indiana.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Romeo Langford - Men's Basketball|url=https://iuhoosiers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/romeo-langford/11003|access-date=2022-02-09|website=Indiana University Athletics|language=en}}</ref>

==College career==
Langford, who was [[ESPN]]'s No. 1 [[shooting guard]] in the Class of 2018 and Indiana's [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]], played one college season in his home state at [[Indiana University]]. Langford tore a [[ligament]] in his thumb in late November at IU, but continued to play through the injury.<ref name="boston.com">{{Cite web |title=5 things to know about Celtics pick Romeo Langford {{!}} Boston.com |url=https://www.boston.com/sports/boston-celtics/2019/06/21/romeo-langford-college-stats-highlights-injury/ |access-date=January 16, 2020 |website=www.boston.com |language=en-US}}</ref> Langford was named [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] Freshman of the Week four times.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://bigten.org/news/2019/1/14/indiana-and-maryland-earn-weekly-mens-basketball-honors.aspx?path=mbball |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190207015430/https://bigten.org/news/2019/1/14/indiana-and-maryland-earn-weekly-mens-basketball-honors.aspx?path=mbball |url-status=dead |archive-date=February 7, 2019 |title=Indiana and Maryland Earn Weekly Men's Basketball Honors |work=Big Ten |date= January 14, 2019 |access-date= February 4, 2019}}</ref> He averaged 16.5 points per game, the highest among Big Ten freshmen and the third highest all-time among Indiana University freshmen, behind [[Eric Gordon]] and [[Mike Woodson]].<ref>Ohio State @ IU CBS Broadcast, February 10, 2019</ref>

After the season, Langford declared for the [[2019 NBA draft]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/26439940/indiana-freshman-langford-says-enter-draft|title = Indiana freshman Langford says he'll enter draft|date = April 4, 2019}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Boston Celtics (2019–2022)===
Langford was selected with the 14th overall draft pick by the [[Boston Celtics]] in the [[2019 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-draft-langford-williams-edwards-waters|title=Celtics Draft Langford, Williams, Edwards & Waters|date=June 21, 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=June 21, 2019}}</ref> On July 11, 2019, Langford signed his rookie scale contract with the Celtics.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-sign-pair-first-round-draft-picks|title=Celtics Sign Pair of First-Round Draft Picks Langford, Williams officially join Celtics|date=July 11, 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 11, 2019}}</ref> Langford was assigned to the [[Maine Celtics|Maine Red Claws]] for the start of the [[NBA G League]] season. He rolled his ankle in a game against the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] on November 15.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Himmelsbach |first1=Adam |title=Romeo Langford hurts ankle in Red Claws game |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/sports/celtics/2019/11/17/romeo-langford-hurts-ankle-red-claws-game/OcrEUKahevOWs0W14ew9FO/story.html |access-date=November 26, 2019 |work=[[Boston Globe]] |date=November 17, 2019}}</ref> On September 22, 2020, the Celtics announced that Langford had undergone surgery to repair the [[scapholunate ligament]] of his right wrist and would miss the remainder of the [[2019–20 NBA season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/romeo-langford-injury-update|title=Romeo Langford Injury Update|date=September 22, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=September 22, 2020}}</ref>

After his injury-riddled rookie season, Langford made his sophomore debut on April 4, 2021, against the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.masslive.com/celtics/2021/04/romeo-langford-shows-defensive-potential-in-celtics-season-debut-hes-going-to-be-key.html|title = Romeo Langford shows defensive potential in Celtics' season debut|date = April 5, 2021}}</ref> He continued to be a semi-constant rotation player for the rest of the season and showed intriguing signs of future potential in the 18 regular season games he played. As injuries continued to plague the Celtics into the 2021 NBA playoffs, Langford took on a larger role. In four of the five playoff games for Boston, he averaged more than 27 minutes per game. With the absences of [[Jaylen Brown]], [[Kemba Walker]], and [[Robert Williams III|Robert Williams]], Langford's expanded playoff opportunity showed glimpses of individual progression, notably in Game 5 against the [[Brooklyn Nets]] where he dropped a playoff career-high 17 points to go along with two steals and two blocks.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/celtics-romeo-langford-drops-career-high-17-points-in-loss/|title = Celtics' Romeo Langford: Drops career-high 17 points in loss| date=June 2, 2021 }}</ref>

Langford played for the Celtics in the [[2021 NBA summer league|2021 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Boston Celtics vs Atlanta Hawks Aug 8, 2021 Box Scores {{!}} NBA.com|url=https://www.nba.com/game/bos-vs-atl-1522100001/box-score#box-score|access-date=2021-08-08|website=www.nba.com}}</ref> On December 31, 2021, he scored a season-high 16 points, alongside three rebounds and two steals, in a 123–108 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=BROWN, SMART STAR AS CELTICS BEAT SUNS 123-108 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100529 |access-date=February 4, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

===San Antonio Spurs (2022–2023)===
On February 10, 2022, Langford was traded, alongside [[Josh Richardson]], to the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in exchange for [[Derrick White]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Fifth-year guard joins Boston backcourt; Langford, Richardson, 2022 protected first-round draft pick to San Antonio|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-acquire-derrick-white-spurs|website=NBA.com|date=February 10, 2022|access-date=February 10, 2022}}</ref> Langford made his Spurs debut on March 7, scoring seven points in a 117–110 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Raul|last=Dominguez|title=SPURS' POPOVICH TIES NELSON FOR NBA CAREER WINS RECORD|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100973|website=NBA.com|date=March 8, 2022|access-date=February 4, 2023}}</ref>

On December 29, 2022, Langford scored a career-high 23 points, alongside three rebounds, two assists and two steals, in a 122–115 win over the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Raul|last=Dominguez|title=SPURS OVERCOME RANDLE'S 41, HAND KNICKS FIFTH STRAIGHT LOSS|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200527|website=NBA.com|date=December 29, 2022|access-date=February 4, 2023 }}</ref>

===Salt Lake City Stars (2023-2024)===
On August 30, 2023, Langford signed with the [[Utah Jazz]],<ref>{{cite web|first=Jeremy|last=Rincon|title=Utah Jazz Sign Kinsey, Langford, and Ongenda|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-kinsey-langford-and-ongenda|website=NBA.com|date=August 30, 2023|access-date=August 30, 2023}}</ref> but was waived on October 17.<ref>{{cite web|first=Gabby|last=Hundman|title=Utah Jazz Waive Devoe, Justice, and Langford|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-waive-devoe-justice-and-langford|website=NBA.com|date=October 17, 2023|access-date=October 18, 2023}}</ref> On October 30, he joined the [[Salt Lake City Stars]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Stars Announce 2023-24 Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/stars-announce-2023-24-training-camp-roster/n-6027250|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 30, 2023|access-date=January 26, 2024}}</ref> In the 2023–24 season for SLC, including both regular season and tip-off tournament, Langford played in 30 games (22 starts).  In the regular season he averaged 29.5 minutes, scoring 11.9 points and 4.1 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web |title=Romeo Langford G-League Stats |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/gleague/players/l/langfro01d.html |website=Basketball-Reference}}</ref>

===BCM Gravelines-Dunkerque (2024)===
On October 29, 2024, Langford signed for six weeks with [[BCM Gravelines-Dunkerque]] of the [[LNB Élite]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Romeo Langford en pigiste médical!|url=http://www.bcmbasket.com/romeo-langford-en-pigiste-medical/|website=BCMBasket.com|date=October 29, 2023|access-date=October 30, 2024|language=french|archive-date=November 1, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241101071501/http://www.bcmbasket.com/romeo-langford-en-pigiste-medical/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On November 29, Langford and BCM Gravelines-Dunkerque mutually agreed to terminate his contract.<ref>{{cite web |title=Romeo Langford n'est plus Maritime ❌ |url=https://x.com/BCMBasket/status/1862445474394890515 |website=X |publisher=BCM Basketball |access-date=January 13, 2026 |language=French |date=November 29, 2024}}</ref>

& A: Langford's mother, Sabrina Langford |work=insidethehall.com |date= May 3, 2018 |access-date= May 3, 2018 |last=Bozich |first=Alex}}</ref> He began playing basketball in the first grade, and has |access-date= November 28, 2017 |last=Makris |first=Stefanos}}</ref> Romeo has expressed pride in challenging himself academically through advanced classes and enjoyment in taking math, and noted that Courier-Journal]] |last=Page |first=Fletcher |date= May 8, 2017 |access-date= November 22, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web
